ai.title: Expand skipped terminal commands
ai.summary: Added 26 shell commands to SKIPPED_TERMINAL_COMMANDS in common/src/constants.ts. CLI logic in npm-app/src/cli.ts now imports this shared constant instead of using a local hardcoded array. Scope covers CLI terminal handling and shared constants. Match logic uses startsWith on lowercase input.

eli5.text: The terminal command list just got bigger. When you type a command into the terminal, the system checks it against a predefined list of commands to determine if it should be skipped or processed. The change adds 26 more commands to this list, including common ones like date, head, history, jobs, less, man, more, nice, read, set, sort, split, tail, test, time, top, touch, type, unset, what, which, who, write, and yes. This means if you use any of these commands, the system will now recognize them and handle them appropriately according to its rules.

ai.title: Add maxTokens parameter to Claude API calls
ai.summary: Claude API functions now accept optional maxTokens parameter, defaulting to 4096. Anthropic SDK updated to 0.27.1. Added cache_control support to message schema and assert utility function.

eli5.text: The assistant can now be told to give shorter or longer answers before you ever see them, and by default it keeps roughly the same length it does today. If someone building with the assistant chooses a response size, that limit is now respected instead of always falling back to a fixed number; the system also gained a small helper for catching mistakes early and a checkbox that lets a message be reused for a short time without paying for it again. Nothing about the assistant you interact with looks different unless one of those builders turns the new setting on.

ai.title: Remove chain of thought from system prompt
ai.summary: Removed brainstorming, uncertainty scoring, and code review steps from system prompt. Simplified file request logic and terminal command failure handling. Affects backend/src/system-prompt.ts.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal instructions were trimmed: it no longer writes out its own private brainstorming notes, no longer assigns itself a certainty score to decide whether to pause, and no longer drafts a step-by-step plan before acting. If you watched it work today, you'd see it move straight from reading your request to requesting any needed files and then to making edits or running commands, rather than first writing out a deliberation about which approach to take. It does still stop and ask for clarification if two attempts at a task have already failed, but that's now the only built-in pause.

ai.title: main-prompt.ts accumulate fileContent in onFile callback
ai.summary: backend/src/main-prompt.ts onFile callback now appends fileContent to fullResponse. Fixes missing file content in the final aggregated response. Scope limited to backend main-prompt logic. Accumulation occurs before processFileBlock push, ensuring content is captured even if async processing delays.

eli5.text: When the assistant reads a file you asked about, it now keeps every file's contents together so nothing goes missing from the final reply. Previously, file contents were processed but not saved into the running response, which could leave parts out of what the assistant ultimately returns. This only affects how the assistant gathers and holds file text behind the scenes, so you would notice that replies now include complete file content when they should.
